# frostmoln_vpc (Resource)

Manages a VPC in the Frostmoln Cloud Platform.

**A VPC created through Terraform is an ISOLATED network until a `frostmoln_gateway` is declared for it.** This resource deliberately carries no connectivity choice: in Terraform the choice IS the presence, absence and `mode` of that separate resource, so a VPC with no `frostmoln_gateway` has no outbound internet path — and no inbound one either.

Platform DNS resolution and managed-service control-plane connectivity are reached over routes that exist only while the gateway does, so they are absent too. Instances in a gateway-less VPC cannot resolve names and cannot fetch anything from the internet — which is what makes a `user_data` cloud-init step that installs packages or calls an external endpoint fail on first boot. A managed database, cache or message broker that is deployed INTO this VPC still answers on its private address: that traffic stays inside the VPC and never crosses the gateway, though reaching it by name does need DNS. This is not a fault to diagnose; it is what a VPC is before its outbound path is declared.

Declare a `frostmoln_gateway` with `vpc_id` set to this VPC to give it that path — see the example below and the `frostmoln_gateway` resource. Connectivity is a stated choice, never one a VPC acquires because a field was omitted.

One thing to know before you conclude the gateway is missing: associating a public IP with an instance in the VPC makes the platform attach a gateway implicitly, because a public IP cannot work without one. Egress then starts working for the WHOLE VPC, not just that instance, and the gateway reports `origin` = "implicit_public_ip". It is a real gateway that Terraform did not declare — so prefer declaring `frostmoln_gateway` explicitly, and see that resource for how an implicit gateway and an explicit one interact.

**Authoritative scope** — who owns what on this resource, declared in `internal/scopedecl` and machine-checked against the schema.

**Enacted and reconciled** — every configurable attribute not listed below: the platform applies it, and a refresh reads the truth back.

**Create-immutable** — `cidr`: the platform does not renumber a VPC in place.

**Create-only, change refused (not replaced)** — `dns_label`: the platform freezes the label at create and refuses any other value, and replacing a VPC destroys everything in it — so a change is warned about at plan and refused at apply instead (unset, the platform derives it from the name).

**Observed, not enacted** — `dns_domain`: platform-assigned from the DNS label and the tenant and organization; null until assigned, fixed once it is. `tags_all`: keys set outside Terraform — in the portal, by the fm CLI, or stamped by the platform — appear only here and are kept on every apply, never removed.

**Platform-invented default** — the tenant's default VPC (`is_default`): **keep-with-docs**. Readable as the computed `is_default`; no `default_*` resource exists to adopt it today.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An ISOLATED VPC. This is what a VPC is on its own: no outbound internet, no
# inbound, and — because they are reached over the same path — no platform DNS
# resolution and no managed-service connectivity either. Nothing is missing from
# this configuration; a VPC simply has no connectivity until one is declared for
# it, and there is no argument here that turns it on.
resource "frostmoln_vpc" "isolated" {
  name        = "isolated-vpc"
  description = "Backend VPC with no internet path"
  cidr        = "10.1.0.0/16"

  tags = {
    environment = "production"
  }
}

# A CONNECTED VPC. The outbound path is its own resource, frostmoln_gateway,
# pointed at the VPC. Declare it and instances in the VPC get internet egress,
# platform DNS resolution and managed-service connectivity; leave it out and they
# get none of the three — which is what makes a cloud-init step that installs
# packages or calls an external endpoint fail on first boot.
resource "frostmoln_vpc" "example" {
  name        = "production-vpc"
  description = "Production VPC"
  cidr        = "10.0.0.0/16"

  # Optional. The internal DNS label, fixed at create: unset, it is derived from
  # name ("production-vpc"). Changing it later is refused, never a replacement.
  dns_label = "prod"

  # Optional. VMs in the VPC get internal DNS names unless this is false
  # (unset = the platform default, on). Updates in place.
  # enable_dns_hostnames = false

  tags = {
    environment = "production"
  }
}

resource "frostmoln_gateway" "example" {
  vpc_id = frostmoln_vpc.example.id
  mode   = "public_ip"
}

# With no public_ip_id the platform draws the gateway an address itself — fine
# when nothing outside the VPC needs to know what its traffic comes from. Name a
# frostmoln_public_ip instead when a partner allow-list or a DNS record does.
# See the frostmoln_gateway resource for that, and for the
# acknowledge_connectivity_loss guard that removing a gateway requires.

# tags holds only what this configuration sets; tags_all adds the provider's
# default_tags and any tag set outside this configuration.
output "production_vpc_tags" {
  value = frostmoln_vpc.example.tags_all
}

# The VPC's internal DNS domain (trailing dot), e.g.
# prod.<tenant>.<org>.fm.internal. Instances resolve as <hostname>.<domain>
# from inside this VPC only.
output "production_vpc_dns_domain" {
  value = frostmoln_vpc.example.dns_domain
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cidr` (String) The CIDR block for the VPC.
- `name` (String) The name of the VPC.

### Optional

- `description` (String) A description of the VPC.
- `dns_label` (String) The VPC's DNS label, the first part of its internal DNS domain. Unset, the platform derives it from `name` (diacritics transliterated, lowercased, other characters become `-`, at most 63; `vpc` if nothing is left) and a derived label never fails: one already used in the tenant gets `-2`, `-3`. Set explicitly, it must be an RFC 1123 label (a-z, 0-9, `-`, at most 63) free in the tenant, or the create fails with `VPCDNSLabelTaken`.

    **Fixed at create.** Renaming the VPC never changes it, and a change to this attribute is REFUSED (a warning at plan, an error at apply, before anything is sent) rather than planned as a replacement: replacing a VPC destroys everything in it. To use another label, create a new VPC.
- `enable_dns_hostnames` (Boolean) Whether VMs in the VPC get internal DNS names (`hostname` / `fqdn` on `frostmoln_instance`). Defaults to `true` (the platform's default) when unset; a configuration that never sets it never changes it. Controls VM names only — managed instances are always named. Updates in place; turning it off removes the VPC's VM records.
- `tags` (Map of String) Tags for the VPC. Merged with the provider's `default_tags` on every write (a key set here wins). Holds only the keys this configuration sets; the full set is in `tags_all`.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) The creation timestamp.
- `dns_domain` (String) The VPC's internal DNS domain, `<dns_label>.<tenant>.<org>.fm.internal.` (with a trailing dot; the tenant and organization parts are opaque ids, never names). Instances in the VPC resolve as `<hostname>.<dns_domain>` from inside this VPC only. Assigned by the platform and fixed once assigned; null until then.
- `id` (String) The unique identifier of the VPC.
- `is_default` (Boolean) Whether this is the default VPC.
- `status` (String) The status of the VPC.
- `subnet_count` (Number) The number of subnets in the VPC.
- `tags_all` (Map of String) Every tag the platform holds on this resource: the provider's `default_tags`, this resource's own `tags` (which win on a shared key), and any key set outside Terraform — in the portal, by the fm CLI, or stamped by the platform. Keys set outside Terraform appear only here and are kept on every apply, never removed.
- `updated_at` (String) The last update timestamp.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) How long the provider waits for the create operation to converge before giving up (e.g. "45m", "2h").
- `delete` (String) How long the provider waits for the delete to complete before giving up (e.g. "30m").
- `update` (String) How long the provider waits for an update (resize, in-place change) to converge before giving up (e.g. "30m").
